header: Date: 2026-08-28 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 62m | Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Evan Liu (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (Stratus Head of Platform), Leah Cho (SRE), Anita Patel (Product), Tom Becker (ML infra)
summary: Kickoff for a 2-week POC to capture workload telemetry, create a traffic heatmap, and run burst profiling. Primary goals: validate latency SLO at 95p, measure cost/throughput tradeoffs, and recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private topology. Agreement on telemetry export and initial benchmark plan; next steps to exchange artifacts and schedule run windows.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): alright everyone thanks for joining today, quick check on audio. can you all hear me?
[00:04] Marco (Stratus): yes, loud and clear, thanks Jordan.
[00:07] Jordan: cool. objective for today's sync is to scope the POC: get a telemetry dump, define QPS and concurrency targets, decide the benchmark phases and agree success criteria. we'll also map out timelines.
[00:19] Leah (SRE): sounds good. to be honest our traffic is weird - steady low qps for most of the day but we get 10-12 minute bursts around promotional emails, and sometimes a bunch of bots hammering endpoints.
[00:31] Priya (Redwood SE): ok that's useful. when you say 10-12 minute bursts, what's peak qps during those windows?
[00:36] Leah: peak is usually 350-420 QPS on the inference layer, sustained around 3-5 minutes then tailing for another 7-8. avg across day is about 40 qps.
[00:48] Evan (Redwood): do you have per-route breakdown? a single customer flow or many small queries?
[00:52] Tom (ML infra): majority is single-turn product-description completions - one prompt in, one generated long output. avg input tokens ~35, output tokens ~180 but there is a long tail up to 800 tokens for certain recommendation outputs.
[01:07] Jordan: good — that token skew matters a lot for batching and KV cache sizing. for the POC we'll need sample prompt set with token length distribution and a 7-day traffic histogram.
[01:16] Anita (Product): timeline question — you said POC was two weeks in your email? is that still realistic given the telemetry and coordination?
[01:22] Jordan: yes two-week nominal window. week 1 is data capture/bench design + small baseline runs, week 2 is full stress + sustained soak and regression. if we need private infra for compliance that can add time but we can start with hosted tests and simulated VPC latency.
[01:36] Marco: our compliance team would prefer VPC/private but we can run initial perf on hosted as long as data doesn't persist. encryption at rest and KMS is required.
[01:44] Priya: we can do that — Redwood Hosted POC with ephemeral logs and KMS bindings for the test runs. we'll outline the binding steps in the runbook.
[01:52] Leah: on success criteria, what metrics do you recommend we lock to? 95th latency, error rate, and cost per 1k tokens?
[01:58] Jordan: typical matrix I recommend: 95th token latency < 800ms for the 180-token outputs for standard routes, p99 < 1.5s (we'll show both with and without batching), error rate < 0.5% under peak, and cost target we can model with Redwood Optimize recommendations. also throughput headroom: ability to handle 1.5x observed peak without >20% increase in p95.
[02:20] Tom: heads-up our SLA for customers is 2s p95 right now, so anything under that is acceptable but we'd prefer <1s if possible.
[02:27] Evan: noted. during the benchmark we should test both cold-start scenarios and warm cache—prefix/KV cache hit changes impacts latencies a lot.
[02:35] Marco: yes we've seen warm cache bring p95 from 1.2s to 300-400ms.
[02:39] Jordan: perfect, we'll include warm/cold phases. now let's nail down QPS/concurrency matrix for the run. suggested baseline: 1x = 420 qps (observed peak), 3x stress = 1,260 qps with burst traffic profile, and soak at 1.5x = 630 qps for 4 hours. does that sound right?
[02:56] Leah: 3x is aggressive but good to see failure modes. also we want to simulate token skew — 80% of requests small (<100 tokens), 15% medium (100-300), 5% large (>300).
[03:08] Priya: that token distribution will affect batching windows and the effective throughput. we'll create two load-scripst: one that preserves your real-world skew, another worst-case that amplifies large-token proportion to 15% to exercise memory/kv pressure.
[03:21] Marco: can you also test model variants? sometimes we route to a smaller quantized model for cheap inference. we'd like to understand quality vs cost tradeoffs.
[03:28] Jordan: yes we'll include at least two model profiles: a high-accuracy baseline (float or 8-bit quant) and a cost-optimized quantized variant. Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization settings.
[03:36] Anita: what about dedicated vs hosted capacity? If we see consistent peaks, we may need reserved capacity. can you help with capacity sizing?
[03:44] Evan: absolutely — after we run the POC we'll deliver a sizing recommendation with expected GPU hours and cost estimates for Dedicated pools. we'll provide a chart mapping QPS/concurrency to GPU count and expected p95.
[03:54] Leah: security checklist — SSO/SAML, SOC2 reports, audit logs, and KMS. also we are in eu-west so data residency matters.
[04:03] Priya: we have SOC2 docs and EU regions; for the POC we can use eu-west hosted endpoints and enable KMS. we'll attach the compliance pack to the runbook.
[04:11] Tom: one more - does Redwood support tracing token-level cost breakdowns per request? we'll need that for our billing alignment.
[04:18] Jordan: yes console exposes token breakdown per request and per model. we'll show a sample report during the benchmark review.
[04:24] Marco: good. about the telemetry export - what format do you need?
[04:27] Priya: a csv or parquet with timestamp, route, request_size_tokens, response_size_tokens, latency_ms, status, user_tier, and maybe a prompt hash. 7 days preferred. if you have synthetic traces from past campaigns that help.
[04:39] Marco: we can do csv. we'll pull last 30 days and sample the last 7 days for the POC.
[04:44] Jordan: great. benchmark phases recap — Phase A baseline (real traffic replay at 1x) to validate metrics; Phase B stress (3x bursts at configured burst windows) to find failure modes; Phase C soak (sustained 1.5x for 4-8 hours) to test memory leaks & degradation. plus warm/cold cache sub-phases and model variant comparison.
[05:05] Anita: do you need us to provide any credentials or open firewall ports?
[05:08] Priya: if you run hosted experiments we just need an API key and optional VPC peering details for private test. detailed steps will be in the runbook. we never keep customer test data after the POC.
[05:19] Leah: about observability — can you emit real-time dashboards during the run? we want charts on QPS, p95, p99, downstream GPU utilization, and token mix.
[05:27] Evan: yes we'll stand up a dashboard for the POC and give read-only access.
[05:30] Jordan: ok great. now pain points: Marco, earlier you said bots - do you need fingerprinting or rate policies applied?
[05:37] Marco: ideally we want to understand the bot signature first. for POC just replay as we saw it; later we'd like rate-limiting recommendations to protect models.
[05:44] Jordan: makes sense — we'll note that as a follow-up.
[05:47] (brief cross talk)
[05:50] Priya: one operational note: for the 3x stress run we will throttle client-side when backend errors exceed threshold to avoid cascading failures; we'll capture error traces for root cause.
[05:59] Tom: curious about cost modelling — can you give an expected cost per million tokens for hosted vs dedicated?
[06:03] Jordan: we'll produce a cost model in the POC report — rough numbers during call: hosted with our balanced model ~ $X per 1M tokens, dedicated with quantized models substantially lower per token but with reserved GPU cost amortized. we'll send a sample spreadsheet.
[06:16] Marco: ok. last piece: success criteria concrete bullets?
[06:19] Jordan: yes — 1) p95 for standard route < 1s on warm cache, 2) system handles 1.5x peak for 4h w/o p95 exceeding 1.5x baseline, 3) error rate < 0.5% under peak, 4) reproducible cost forecast showing >=20% saving with recommended config (if applicable), 5) security checklist validated for hosted eu-west test.
[06:39] Anita: sounds reasonable, can we add stakeholder signoff step to close the POC?
[06:43] Jordan: yes we'll include a stakeholder review and signoff doc at the end of week 2.
[06:46] Marco: thanks everyone — next steps then are artifact exchange and schedule.
[06:49] Jordan: i'll send the benchmark template and runbook links by Wednesday (2026-09-02) and Priya will share load scripts. Leah you'll send telemetry by Friday (2026-09-04). any final questions?
[06:59] Leah: none.
[07:01] Tom: no.
[07:03] Jordan: great, thanks all. we'll follow up in email with links and the calendar invites for the runs.
[07:08] (meeting ends)
notes: Call included technical details for QPS matrix, token distribution, cold/warm cache impacts, and an agreed 3-phase benchmark. Slight transcription errors present (names and acronyms occasionally mis-heard). Planned POC window: 2 weeks with artifact exchange by 2026-09-04.
